items: dict keyed by edt_01, edt_02, ... — one per section, in narrative order.
label: short name for this section.
purpose: one of hook, context, evidence, turn, close.
title: section title for display (null if no title).
findings: array of ana_xx IDs this section draws on, ordered by importance.
context: array of det_xx IDs that provide background for this section.
triage: maps each ana_xx used in this section to its role (lead / supporting / color).
chart_placeholder: the ana_xx ID whose data_table should drive the main chart in this section (null if no chart).
media_placeholder: media type hint — one of 'map', 'video', 'image', 'audio', 'interactive', 'instance', or null if no non-text media is genuinely useful. Never write boolean true or a vague string like 'media'.
editorial_notes: constraints the Designer and Programmer must respect (exact numbers, visible caveats, etc.).
full_triage: maps EVERY ana_xx ID from analyst.json to its editorial role (lead / supporting / color / cut). This ensures nothing is silently dropped.
interactives: top-level object {hero, supporting[]} curated from the Imagineer pool (imagineer.json img_xx) — the binding set the Interaction Engineer builds (NOT just an editorial hint like media_placeholder). Present whenever any interactive is warranted.
interactives.hero: the ONE centerpiece object, REQUIRED (non-null) when ANY interactive is warranted; null only when the piece has no interactive at all (e.g. an abstract dataset where the Imagineer stayed light). Fields: concept_ref (the img_xx being realized, or null if nominating a hero the Imagineer didn't propose), finding (the ana_xx the reader produces), purpose (INFORM|IMMERSE), section (the edt_xx it lives in), archetype, why_hero (one line: why this is the single contestable headline the reader must produce). It is the same finding as the prose centerpiece nomination.
interactives.supporting: a ranked array of additional playgrounds, each earning its place; [] when only the hero is warranted. The cap is QUALITATIVE, NEVER numeric — keep every concept that makes the reader produce a DISTINCT finding, cut every one that re-teaches a finding already delivered. More is not better; an unearned widget is decoration.
interactives.supporting[].finding: the ana_xx this playground makes hands-on. MUST be DISTINCT: no two supporting entries may share an ana_xx, and none may share the hero's finding. A duplicate finding is the signal to cut, not rank.
interactives.supporting[].purpose: INFORM (reader produces a number/insight the prose can't hand over) or IMMERSE (reader produces a feeling — the correction lands). A supporting entry that is neither does not earn its place.
interactives.supporting[].concept_ref: the Imagineer img_xx this realizes, or null if curating a concept the Imagineer didn't propose. img_xx is internal — it is never tagged on the page.
interactives.supporting[].section: the edt_xx section this playground lives in.
interactives.supporting[].archetype: the interaction archetype (from interaction_playbook.json interaction_taxonomy): explorable_recompute / tune_the_assumption / guess_then_reveal / scored_quiz / personal_input / playable_game / scrollytelling.
interactives.supporting[].rank: integer priority, 1 = strongest. Lets the Builder/Critic reason about which supporting elements matter most if scope must be trimmed.
interactives.supporting[].earns_place: one line: the DISTINCT finding this makes hands-on and why it is not a duplicate of the hero or another supporting. This is the qualitative gate — if you can't state it, cut the entry.
